test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 6 Sept 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Article 18 of the Indian Constitution deals with which of the following rights?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Abolition of titles**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Abolition of titles**

 
 
• Article 18 comes under the Right to equality.
 
• It tells about the abolition of titles except military and academic.​
 
 

 
 

 Right to equality (Article 14-18)
 Consists of 
 
 

 Article 14
 Equality before law and equal protection of laws.
 
 

 Article 15 
 Prohibition of discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth 
 
 

 Article 16
 Equality of opportunity in matters of public employment. 
 
 

 Article 17
 Abolition of untouchability and prohibition of its practice.
 
 

 Article 18
 Abolition of titles except military and academic.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Cultural and Educational Rights safeguard the rights of linguistic, cultural, and religious minorities.
 
 
• Preserving culture and heritage is vital in this scenario.
 
• To ensure that education is provided for everyone without any kind of discrimination, Education Rights was formulated.
 
 
 
• Right against exploitation is a Fundamental Right.
 
 
• Right against Exploitation is in Articles 23 – 24.
 
• Article 23 states the Prohibition of traffic in human beings and forced labor.
 
• Article 24 states the Prohibition of employment of children in factories, etc.
 
 
 
• Right to Freedom (Articles 19 - 22):
 
 
• Freedom is one of the most important ideals cherished by any democratic society.
 
• The Indian Constitution guarantees freedom to citizens.
 
• The freedom right includes many rights such as:
 
 
• Freedom of speech.
 
• Freedom of expression.
 
• Freedom of assembly without arms.
 
• Freedom of association.
 
• Freedom to practice any profession.
 
• Freedom to reside in any part of the country.
